points.text: Writes the digits of the lakh, thousand and hundred places with correct values
Writes the tens and ones values correctly to complete the expanded form

scheme.common_error: Writing the digits as place names or without their place value, e.g. 3 + 5 + 6 + 2 + 8

Short Questions.question: A factory makes 13,206 bottles each day. How many bottles does it make in 6 days?

points.text: Chooses and sets up a correct method to find the total
Correct answer 79,236 bottles

accept: Repeated addition of 13,206 six times giving 79,236
scheme.common_error: Carrying incorrectly when multiplying, e.g. 78,236

Short Questions.question: Which fraction is greater, 2/3 or 3/5? Show your working.

points.text: A correct method for the common denominator and equivalent fractions
States that 2/3 is greater

scheme.common_error: Comparing only the numerators or denominators, e.g. saying 3/5 is greater because 3 > 2

Short Questions.question: Hira has 18 apples and 30 oranges. They pack them into baskets with the same number of fruits in each basket and only one kind of fruit in each basket. What is the largest number of fruits in each basket?
Short Questions.answer: HCF of 18 and 30 = 6. Each basket holds 6 fruits.

points.text: A correct method to find the highest common factor
Correct answer 6 fruits

scheme.common_error: Finding the LCM (90) instead of the HCF

Short Questions.question: Zara has 2/5 of a cake. She eats 1/4 of that part. What fraction of the whole cake does Zara eat?

points.text: Multiplies the numerators and the denominators correctly
Correct answer 1/10 in simplest form

scheme.common_error: Adding the fractions or leaving the answer as 2/20 unsimplified

points.text: A correct method to convert the fraction, such as an equivalent fraction with denominator 10 or 100, or division
Correct answer 0.8

scheme.common_error: Writing 0.45 by placing the numerator and denominator side by side

Short Questions.question: Maryam buys 12.45 m of cloth and 8.3 m of ribbon. What is the total length in metres?

points.text: Chooses addition and lines up the decimal points
Correct answer 20.75 m

accept: Adding whole numbers and decimal parts separately to get 20.75 m
scheme.common_error: Not aligning the decimal points

points.text: Writes the percent as a fraction out of 100 or divides by 100
Correct answer 0.35

accept: Moving the decimal point two places to the left
scheme.common_error: Writing 3.5 or 0.035

Short Questions.question: Five bags weigh 7 kg, 10 kg, 6 kg, 8 kg and 9 kg. Find the average weight of a bag in kilograms.

points.text: A correct method: adds all the weights and divides by the number of bags
Correct answer 8 kg

scheme.common_error: Dividing the sum by 4 or 6 instead of 5

Short Questions.question: Draw an angle of 125° with a protractor.
Short Questions.answer: A drawn angle measuring 125°, an obtuse angle, with the vertex at the centre point of the protractor.

points.text: Draws a base ray and places the protractor correctly on the vertex with the 0 on the ray
Marks 125° and draws the second ray to form the angle accurately

accept: Angle drawn opening to the right using the bottom scale
Angle drawn opening to the left using the top scale
scheme.common_error: Reading the wrong scale and drawing an angle of 55°

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: A school fund holds Rs. 604,309. Write this amount in words and in expanded form.
Word Problems.answer: In words: six hundred four thousand, three hundred nine. Expanded form: 600,000 + 4,000 + 300 + 9.

points.text: Writes the thousands part correctly in words
Writes the hundreds, tens and ones part correctly in words to complete the number name
Writes the correct expanded form with the right place values of every non-zero digit

accept: six hundred and four thousand, three hundred and nine
scheme.common_error: Writes the number name as six hundred forty thousand three hundred nine, or writes 40,000 instead of 4,000 in the expanded form.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: Subtract 358,967 from 826,450 using the vertical method.

points.text: Writes the numbers in correct place value columns with the larger number on top
Regroups correctly in the columns where the top digit is smaller
Gets the correct difference 467,483

scheme.common_error: Subtracts the smaller digit from the larger digit in each column instead of regrouping, getting a wrong difference.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following word problem. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: A school fair has a budget of Rs. 1,000,000. The school pays Rs. 438,250 for stalls and Rs. 276,340 for lights. How much money is left in the budget?

points.text: Chooses to add the two payments to find the total paid
Adds correctly to get Rs. 714,590
Chooses to subtract the total paid from the budget
Subtracts correctly and gives the answer Rs. 285,410 with the unit

accept: Subtract 438,250 from 1,000,000 and then subtract 276,340 from the result to get Rs. 285,410
Add the payments then subtract from the budget
scheme.common_error: Adds the budget and the payments, or subtracts only one of the two payments from Rs. 1,000,000.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following word problem. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: Two buses leave a station together. One bus leaves every 28 minutes and the other leaves every 42 minutes. Using the division method, find after how many minutes both buses leave together again.
Word Problems.answer: Dividing 28 and 42 by 2, 2, 7, 3 gives 1 and 1. LCM = 2 x 2 x 7 x 3 = 84 minutes.

points.text: Recognises that the LCM of the two times is needed
Sets up the division method correctly with a common prime divisor at each step
Multiplies all the divisors and gives the answer 84 minutes with the unit

accept: Prime factorization method: 28 = 2 x 2 x 7, 42 = 2 x 3 x 7, LCM = 84
Listing common multiples of 28 and 42 until 84
scheme.common_error: Finds the HCF 14 instead of the LCM, or multiplies 28 by 42 to get 1,176.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following word problem. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: A tanker holds 53,486 litres of water. The water is poured equally into tanks that each hold 56 litres. How many tanks are filled completely and how many litres of water are left over?
Word Problems.answer: 53,486 / 56 = 955 remainder 6. 955 tanks are filled and 6 litres are left over.

points.text: Chooses division of 53,486 by 56
Carries out the long division steps correctly
Gives the quotient 955 tanks
Gives the remainder 6 litres with the unit

accept: Repeated subtraction of multiples of 56 reaching 955 and remainder 6
scheme.common_error: Ignores the remainder or gives a quotient of 956 by rounding up.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following word problem. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: A school buys 18,764 chairs. Each chair is priced at Rs. 47. How much money does the school pay in total?

points.text: Chooses to multiply the number of chairs by the price of one chair
Multiplies correctly by the ones digit to get 131,348
Multiplies correctly by the tens digit to get 750,560, placing the zero
Adds the partial products and gives Rs. 881,908 with the unit

accept: Partial products 18,764 x 7 and 18,764 x 40 added
scheme.common_error: Forgets the zero when multiplying by the tens digit, giving 75,056 instead of 750,560.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following word problem. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: Sara has four ribbons of lengths 5/8 m, 7/12 m, 3/4 m and 2/3 m. Arrange the lengths from the shortest to the longest.

points.text: Finds a correct common denominator for the four fractions
Converts all four fractions to equivalent fractions correctly
Compares the numerators correctly
Writes the correct order from shortest to longest with the unit

accept: Any common denominator that is a multiple of 24
Converting to decimals 0.583, 0.625, 0.667, 0.75 and ordering them
scheme.common_error: Compares only the numerators or only the denominators, so 3/4 m is placed as the shortest.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: Subtract 2 5/6 from 6 1/4.

points.text: Converts both mixed numbers to improper fractions correctly
Uses a correct method for the common denominator
Subtracts the numerators correctly to get 41/12
Writes the answer as the mixed number 3 5/12

accept: Subtracting whole numbers and fractions separately with regrouping: 5 15/12 - 2 10/12 = 3 5/12
Converting to improper fractions then subtracting
scheme.common_error: Subtracts the smaller fraction from the larger one in the wrong order, or subtracts the denominators.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following word problem. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: Bilal buys 3 packets of dates at Rs. 28.75 each. He pays with a Rs. 100 note. How much change does he get back?
Word Problems.answer: Price of 3 packets = 28.75 x 3 = Rs. 86.25. Change = 100 - 86.25 = Rs. 13.75.

points.text: Chooses to multiply the price of one packet by 3
Multiplies correctly, placing the decimal point, to get Rs. 86.25
Chooses to subtract the price from Rs. 100
Subtracts correctly and gives Rs. 13.75 with the unit

accept: Counting up from Rs. 86.25 to Rs. 100
scheme.common_error: Misplaces the decimal point in the product, giving Rs. 862.50 or Rs. 8.625.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: A phone battery shows 35%. Write 35% as a fraction in its simplest form and as a decimal.

points.text: Writes the percentage as a fraction with denominator 100
Simplifies the fraction correctly using a common factor
Gives the simplest form 7/20
Writes the decimal 0.35

accept: Dividing the numerator and denominator by 5 in one step or by steps
scheme.common_error: Leaves the fraction as 35/100 without simplifying or writes the decimal as 3.5.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following word problem. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: A notebook is priced at Rs. 38. Find the price of 14 notebooks.

points.text: States the value of one notebook as the starting point (unitary method)
Chooses to multiply by the number of notebooks
Multiplies correctly to get 532
Gives the answer with the unit Rs.

scheme.common_error: Divides 38 by 14 instead of multiplying.

Word Problems.main_question: Solve the following word problem. Show your steps.
Word Problems.question: A shopkeeper sells 9 kg of rice for Rs. 630. What is the price of 5 kg of rice?

points.text: Chooses to find the price of 1 kg by dividing 630 by 9
Divides correctly to get Rs. 70
Chooses to multiply the price of 1 kg by 5
Multiplies correctly and gives Rs. 350 with the unit

accept: Unitary method through the price of 1 kg
scheme.common_error: Multiplies 630 by 5 and divides by 9 incorrectly, or gives the price of 1 kg (Rs. 70) as the final answer.

Graphs & Geometric Problems.main_question: Draw a bar graph for the given data
Graphs & Geometric Problems.question: The table shows the number of books read by five students in a month. Draw a bar graph to represent the given data.
Graphs & Geometric Problems.answer: A bar graph with a title, labelled axes and an equal scale (for example 1 unit = 5 books). Bars: Ali 20, Sara 35, Hina 15, Omar 40, Zoya 25.

points.text: A suitable equal scale chosen and marked on the axis
Both axes labelled and a title given
All five bars drawn with equal widths and gaps
Bar heights correct for at least 3 values
All five bar heights correct

accept: Vertical bar graph with any equal scale
Horizontal bar graph with any equal scale
scheme.common_error: Using an uneven scale or bars of different widths

Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).main_question: Draw and identify any two of the following angles.
Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).question: Draw and identify any two of the following angles.
Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).answer: Obtuse angle: draw an angle between 90 and 180 degrees, e.g. 120 degrees. Supplementary angle: draw two angles adding to 180 degrees, e.g. 110 degrees and 70 degrees on a straight line. Straight angle: draw a straight line showing 180 degrees.

points.text: First angle drawn correctly with a protractor or a correct method
Second angle drawn correctly with a protractor or a correct method
Both angles named and measures marked correctly

accept: Any obtuse angle between 90 and 180 degrees
Any pair of angles adding up to 180 degrees
scheme.common_error: Drawing an obtuse angle smaller than 90 degrees or a pair that does not add to 180 degrees

Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).question: Find the area of a parallelogram with a base of 12 cm and a height of 7 cm.
Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).answer: Area = base x height = 12 x 7 = 84 cm2

points.text: A correct formula for the area of a parallelogram stated
Correct values substituted in the formula
A correct method for multiplying the base by the height
Correct answer 84
Correct unit chosen (cm2)

scheme.common_error: Adding the base and height or using the slant side instead of the height

Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).question: A rectangular garden is 15 m long and 9 m wide. Find its perimeter.

points.text: A correct formula or method for the perimeter of a rectangle
Correct values substituted
A correct method for adding the lengths
Correct answer 48
Correct unit chosen (m)

scheme.common_error: Multiplying length by width, which gives the area 135

Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).question: A shopkeeper sold 12, 18, 15, 20 and 25 kg of rice on five days. Find the average amount of rice sold each day.

points.text: A correct method for finding the sum of all values
Sum 90 found correctly
Sum divided by the number of values (5)
Correct answer 18 (Correct unit chosen (kg))

accept: Average = sum of observations / number of observations = 18 kg
scheme.common_error: Dividing the sum by the wrong number of values

Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).question: Two angles together make a right angle. One of them is 35 degrees. Find the other angle and name the pair.
Graphs & Geometric Problems (2).answer: Right angle = 90 degrees. Other angle = 90 - 35 = 55 degrees. The pair is complementary angles.

points.text: Right angle recognised as 90 degrees
A correct method for finding the unknown angle
Correct answer 55 degrees
Pair named as complementary angles (Correct unit chosen (degrees))

scheme.common_error: Subtracting from 180 degrees and naming the pair supplementary

header.title_en: Grade 5 · Mathematics · FDE pattern practice paper
header.title_ur: جماعت پنجم · ریاضی · FDE pattern کا مشقی پرچہ
header.note_en: Note: This paper consists of THREE Sections. Section – A needs to be solved on the Question Paper. Section B, C to be solved on the Answer Sheet. Cutting, erasing and overwriting is not allowed.

grain.kind: one concept per item: place value, rounding, factors, fraction and decimal comparison, percent to fraction, unitary cost, area, averages
grain.number_size: whole numbers up to 7 digits; decimals to 3 places; fractions with denominators up to 10

slots.prompt_rule: Twenty four-option MCQs across all included units, one concept each; 3 to 5 of them pure recall (a fact or a name). Never define a term in the stem and then ask what that definition states: the stem must not give away its own answer. Options are short (a number or a few words). The mean (average) appears in at most one item of the whole paper; a Section A statistics item asks the mode, median or range instead. No option states a method.  An MCQ never uses the numbers or fractions that a later compare, order or arrange item uses.Never set an item on a "Create and Connect" or "Discovery Playground" activity unless this slot says so.

grain.kind: one-step skill check, one topic each: expanded form, 5-digit × 1-digit, compare two fractions, HCF of two small numbers, fraction × fraction, fraction to decimal, decimal addition, percent to decimal, average of five numbers, draw an angle
grain.number_size: up to 6 digits; 3-place decimals; denominators 2 to 5

slots.prompt_rule: Ten one-step items, one per topic, in this order of kinds where the pages allow: expanded form; multiplication 5-digit × 1-digit; compare two fractions; HCF of two numbers; fraction × fraction; fraction to decimal; decimal addition; percent to decimal; average of five numbers; "Draw an angle of N° with a protractor." (construction only, never "and name it"). 2 marks each: M1 + A1.  Compare, order and arrange items use fractions no Section A MCQ offers.Never set an item on a "Create and Connect" or "Discovery Playground" activity unless this slot says so.

slots.instruction_en: Attempt any {w:eight} questions. All questions carry equal marks.

grain.kind: 5-mark worked problem: number in words, a budget subtraction, long division by a 2-digit number, long multiplication, LCM by the division method, mixed-number subtraction, a fraction word problem, a decimal word problem, decimal division, a percentage word problem, two unitary-method problems
grain.number_size: up to 7 digits; 5-digit ÷ 2-digit; 5-digit × 2-digit; decimals to 2 places

slots.prompt_rule: Twelve 5-mark items from Units 1–8 as four families of three: for Units 1–2, 3–4, 5–6 and 7–8 one number-sense item, one computation and one word problem each. Include long division, long multiplication, LCM by the division method, a mixed-number subtraction and two unitary-method problems (many from one, one from many). Every word problem names its unit (Rs., km, litres) in the question. Compare, order and arrange items use fractions no Section A MCQ offers.

sections.note_en: Note: Q3 is compulsory. Attempt any {w:three} from the remaining questions. All questions carry 5 marks each. ({n:4} × 5 = {t:20})

grain.kind: draw a bar graph from a 5-row table

slots.prompt_rule: One item: a sentence naming the data, then "Draw a bar graph to represent the given data." Put the data in `table` as {"headers": [label, quantity with unit], "rows": five [label, value]}. Never describe or refer to a printed graph.

grain.kind: one each: draw and identify angles, area, perimeter, average, missing angle

slots.prompt_rule: Five items in this order, one of each kind: draw and identify any two of three named angles (obtuse, supplementary, straight): `question` = "Draw and identify any two of the following angles.", `questions` = exactly three strings, "Obtuse angle", "Supplementary angle", "Straight angle", with no letter or number in front (the paper numbers them i, ii, iii); the area of a parallelogram or a triangle; the perimeter of a rectangle or a square; the average of five values; a missing angle stated in WORDS, on a pair Q4 does not name ("Two angles together make a right angle. One of them is 35°. Find the other angle and name the pair."). The area and perimeter items give every length with its unit (a base of 12 cm), and the answer carries the matching unit (cm², cm). Never send the child to a figure that is not printed. The missing-angle stem never names the relation it asks the child to name.

lines_en: MCQs: 1 mark for the letter. Two circles or an overwritten answer = 0.
M = method · A = answer · U = unit · K = key point · L = label.
A correct answer with no working earns the A mark(s) only (Q1(b): both marks).
A method step with an arithmetic slip keeps half its M marks (round down) if the method is right; later steps that use the slipped number correctly earn full marks, including the final A.
"Attempt any N": tell children to answer exactly N. If more are answered, mark all and keep the best N.
lines_ur: معروضی: درست حرف پر 1 نمبر۔ دو دائرے یا اوور رائٹنگ = 0۔
M = طریقہ، A = جواب، U = اکائی، K = اہم نکتہ، L = نام
بغیر طریقے کے درست جواب پر صرف A نمبر۔
طریقہ درست ہو اور حساب میں چوک ہو تو اس مرحلے کے آدھے M نمبر (کم کی طرف)؛ بعد کے مراحل میں اسی غلط عدد پر درست کام ہو تو پورے نمبر، آخری A سمیت۔
«کوئی سے N»: بچوں کو بالکل N سوال حل کرنے کو کہیں۔ زیادہ حل ہوں تو سب جانچ کر بہترین N رکھیں۔
